questions.q: What do ai_parse_document and ai_extract each do, and in what order do they run?
options: ai_parse_document extracts raw text/tables/layout from a document first; ai_extract then pulls specific structured fields out of that parsed content against a described schema
ai_extract runs first to guess a schema, then ai_parse_document fills in the raw bytes
Both functions do the identical job and are interchangeable in any order
ai_parse_document only works on images, and ai_extract only works on video
questions.explain: ai_parse_document runs first to get usable content out of a raw document; ai_extract runs second to turn that parsed content into specific typed columns against a declared schema.

questions.q: Which medallion layers do the parse and extract steps build, respectively?
options: ai_parse_document builds the Silver layer (parsed content); ai_extract builds the Gold layer (structured, typed fields)
Both functions build only the Bronze layer
ai_parse_document builds Gold directly, skipping Silver entirely
Medallion architecture does not apply to document pipelines at all
questions.explain: Bronze holds raw document bytes from Auto Loader ingestion; Silver is built via ai_parse_document; Gold is built via ai_extract against a declared schema — the same Bronze/Silver/Gold pattern from Chapter 3.

questions.q: What does the 'Use Agent' shortcut generate when given a natural-language description of a document pipeline?
options: A working Declarative Pipeline as real, editable pyspark.pipelines code covering ingestion, parse, and extract steps
A proprietary, non-editable binary pipeline format
Only a PDF report describing what the pipeline would look like, with no actual code
A static SQL view with no ingestion or incremental processing at all
questions.explain: Like Lakeflow Designer in the previous lesson, 'Use Agent' produces real, inspectable pyspark.pipelines code rather than a black box — the same AI-assisted-but-transparent authoring principle.

questions.q: What are the three tasks in Databricks' reference Lakeflow Jobs orchestration pattern for this pipeline, in order?
options: Ingest, then Parse and Extract, then Refresh Dashboard
Refresh Dashboard, then Ingest, then Parse and Extract
Only two tasks exist: Ingest and Extract
Parse and Extract, then Ingest, then nothing further
questions.explain: The three-task fan-out pattern runs Ingest first (Auto Loader brings in raw documents), then Parse and Extract (building Silver and Gold), then Refresh Dashboard once Gold is updated.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say the Document Intelligence pattern 'belongs' in an advanced Databricks course rather than being a brand-new architecture?
options: Because ai_parse_document and ai_extract are ordinary SQL functions called inside the same Auto Loader -> Declarative Pipeline -> Lakeflow Jobs pattern already taught in this course — only the data source (unstructured documents) is new
Because it requires abandoning Unity Catalog governance entirely
Because it replaces Lakeflow Jobs with a completely different orchestration product
Because it only works with streaming data and cannot handle batch ingestion
questions.explain: Nothing about the pipeline mechanics is new — it's the same incremental, governed, Bronze/Silver/Gold discipline from earlier chapters, just applied to a new kind of raw source data.
